questions.prompt: A button ControlTemplate contains only `<Border Background="Red"><TextBlock Text="Fixed Text"/></Border>`. What happens to `<Button Content="Save"/>` and `<Button Content="Delete"/>`?
options: Each button shows its own Content inside the red border
Both show "Fixed Text", because `Button.Content` is ignored
WPF notices the problem and falls back to the default template
They show both their Content and "Fixed Text" side by side
questions.explanation: `ContentPresenter` is the placeholder that displays the control's content. Without it the content is lost, so every button shows the same fixed text and the template is not reusable.

questions.prompt: Inside a ControlTemplate, the Border has `Background="{TemplateBinding Background}"`. What does that mean?
options: Use the `Background` value of the control that is using this template
Bind to a `Background` property on the ViewModel in `DataContext`
Use the `Background` of the parent Window
Copy the `Background` once when the template loads and never update it
questions.explanation: TemplateBinding is a lightweight binding, used only inside a ControlTemplate, that connects the control's public properties to the template visuals: use the value from the control that is using this template.

questions.prompt: A ListBox is bound to a collection of `Person` objects and has no DataTemplate or `DisplayMemberPath`. What does each row show?
options: The `Name` property, because it is the first property
An empty row for every item in the list
A grid with one column per property
The object's full type name (from `ToString()`)
questions.explanation: Without a DataTemplate, controls bound to custom objects display the fully qualified name of each object, or the result of its `ToString()` method.

questions.prompt: You declare `<DataTemplate DataType="{x:Type local:Person}">` in resources with no `x:Key`. What do you need on `<ListBox ItemsSource="{Binding People}" />` for it to be used?
options: `ItemTemplate="{StaticResource Person}"` on the ListBox
`DisplayMemberPath="Person"` so WPF knows which template
Nothing; WPF applies it to `Person` items automatically
A `ContentPresenter` placed inside the ListBox element
questions.explanation: When you omit `x:Key` and set `DataType`, WPF applies the DataTemplate automatically by data type, so the plain `<ListBox ItemsSource="{Binding People}" />` uses it.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson warn against putting a Button ControlTemplate without an `x:Key` in `App.xaml`?
options: It replaces the default template app-wide, which can break other controls
Templates in `App.xaml` are ignored entirely unless they have an `x:Key`
Every Button in the app would lose its `Click` and `Command` behavior
WPF only allows keyed ControlTemplates inside `Application.Resources`
questions.explanation: A keyless ControlTemplate in `App.xaml` replaces the default control template everywhere, which can break third-party controls, remove accessibility features and break focus visuals.

questions.prompt: You only need to change the background color, font and padding of your app's buttons. What should you reach for first?
options: A ControlTemplate, because it is the only way to change colors
A DataTemplate set as the button's `ItemTemplate`
A new custom control class
A Style with Setters
questions.explanation: A Style sets and reuses properties without changing the control's structure; a ControlTemplate rebuilds the visual tree. The lesson's rule is to always try Style first and use ControlTemplate only if Style is not enough.
